dedupe_keys.name: mapping road surface type of kenya using openstreetmap and high resolution google satellite imagery

description: Mapping Road Surface Type of Kenya Using OpenStreetMap and High-resolution Google Satellite Imagery is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Qi Zhou et al. Identifying road surface types (paved or unpaved) can ensure road vehicle safety, reduce energy consumption, and promote economic development. Existing studies identified road surface types by using sensors mounted on mobile devices and high-resolution satellite images that are not openly accessible, which makes it difficult to apply them to large-scale (e.g., national or regional) study areas. Coverage: national (KE); published in 2024. Formats: Shapefile. The data are held in Figshare and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
